external_trigger_note: SUT is the urllib3 HTTP client library, exercised by invoking probe.py (docker compose run) inside the client container; the real urllib3 then performs a genuine cross-ORIGIN HTTP 302 to distinct redirector/attacker sidecar hosts. Trigger to the SUT is CLI, but the security-relevant behavior is real HTTP redirect header handling.

audit.evidence: REAL PyPI urllib3 wheels 1.26.16/1.26.17/1.26.19 installed per client profile; probe drives genuine cross-origin 302, attacker sidecar echoes received headers. Live gate: Cookie leaks flag@v0, blocked@v1; Proxy-Authorization leaks flag@v1 (blocked@v2 per repro). passed=true.

app_purpose: HTTP client library for Python (used by requests, pip, and much of the Python ecosystem)
root_cause: CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information: incomplete sensitive-header strip on cross-origin redirect (credential leak)

flag.resource: sensitive request headers (Cookie / Proxy-Authorization) that urllib3 is supposed to strip when a redirect crosses origin
flag.placement: per-run random ${PCB_FLAG} token injected into the CLIENT's outgoing sensitive header at request time (seed: Cookie; residual: Proxy-Authorization); never in library source
flag.detect: flag token substring appears in the attacker collector sidecar's echo of the headers it actually received after the cross-origin 302 (== header was NOT stripped)

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2023-43804 (fixed 1.26.17): the Cookie request header was not stripped during cross-origin redirects, so Cookie was added to Retry.DEFAULT_REMOVE_HEADERS_ON_REDIRECT (frozenset(['Authorization']) -> frozenset(['Cookie', 'Authorization'])). CVE-2024-37891 (GHSA-34jh-p97f-mpxf, fixed 1.26.19): the Proxy-Authorization header is still not stripped during cross-origin redirects by the SAME remove_headers_on_redirect mechanism, so it was added too (-> frozenset(['Cookie', 'Authorization', 'Proxy-Authorization'])). Two sequential residual-header bypasses of the same cross-origin redirect header-strip allowlist.

provenance.verified: 2026-07-14 on real Docker; flag_oracle.validate_case passed=true; residual (Proxy-Authorization) leaks on V0 and V1, blocked on V2; seed (Cookie) leaks on V0, blocked on V1/V2
provenance.notes: Variant A (same sink = remove_headers_on_redirect drop loop in PoolManager.urlopen). Seed = CVE-2023-43804 Cookie leak; residual = CVE-2024-37891 Proxy-Authorization leak; only the header-name allowlist evolved across versions. GENUINE (not reject): distinct fixed versions (1.26.17 vs 1.26.19), V1!=V0 on seed, original(Cookie)!=residual(Proxy-Authorization) on V1, V1 leaks the residual, V2 blocks it, redirect genuinely cross-origin (redirector host -> attacker host, verified via Host: attacker in the echoed headers).
